requirement: Limit system access to authorized users, processes acting on behalf of authorized users, and devices (including other systems).
responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: CEE accounts are provisioned by identity governance from HR events after U.S.-person verification and manager approval. Employee separations disable accounts automatically. Contractor separations depend on supplier notices entered by hand. Gap: 2 of 60 sampled separations were disabled late (4 and 9 business days), both contractor accounts whose separation notices arrived by email
evidence: Identity governance reports; HR and contractor separation lists; P07 AC-2 results

requirement: Limit system access to the types of transactions and functions that authorized users are permitted to execute.
implementation_statement: PLM, suite, and virtual desktop roles limit users to the projects and functions their job needs; administration is limited to PAM-managed roles
evidence: PLM role matrix; suite admin role export; PAM role report

requirement: Control the flow of CUI in accordance with approved authorizations.
implementation_statement: Information flow is enforced by PLM project folder attributes (ITAR, EAR, program), gateway rules, and suite sharing policies that block external sharing outside approved domains. Gap: 14 PLM project folders migrated from a legacy vault in 2026-04 lacked the ITAR attribute; an EAR-licensed foreign-person engineer opened 3 files in one of them (found 2026-08-11, access removed the same day)
evidence: PLM attribute analytics; gateway rule set; suite sharing policy

requirement: Separate the duties of individuals to reduce the risk of malevolent activity without collusion.
implementation_statement: Separation of duties is built into role design: engineers cannot release their own changes, PLM administrators cannot approve releases, and log administrators are separate from system administrators
evidence: Role design standard; PLM workflow configuration

requirement: Employ the principle of least privilege, including for specific security functions and privileged accounts.
responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Least privilege through role-based access and just-in-time elevation in PAM for all administrators; no standing domain administrator rights
evidence: PAM elevation report; quarterly privileged access certification

requirement: Use non-privileged accounts or roles when accessing nonsecurity functions
responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Administrators use separate privileged identities that PAM checks out; daily work uses non-privileged accounts

requirement: Prevent non-privileged users from executing privileged functions and capture the execution of such functions in audit logs.
implementation_statement: Endpoint privilege management blocks elevation by standard users; privileged functions are logged to the SIEM
evidence: EDR and privilege management policy; SIEM use case list

requirement: Limit unsuccessful logon attempts.
responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Identity platform locks accounts after 5 failed attempts for 15 minutes and alerts the SOC on spray patterns

requirement: Provide privacy and security notices consistent with applicable CUI rules.
responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: CUI system use notices display at sign-in to the identity platform, virtual desktops, and PLM

requirement: Use session lock with pattern-hiding displays to prevent access and viewing of data after a period of inactivity
implementation_statement: Session lock with pattern-hiding after 15 minutes on endpoints and virtual desktops

requirement: Terminate (automatically) a user session after a defined condition.
implementation_statement: Virtual desktop and PLM sessions end after 12 hours or 60 minutes idle; suite tokens expire per conditional access

requirement: Monitor and control remote access sessions.
implementation_statement: Remote access only through the virtual desktop gateway and the CEE remote access service, with sessions logged and monitored by the SOC

requirement: Employ cryptographic mechanisms to protect the confidentiality of remote access sessions.
implementation_statement: Remote sessions use TLS and IPsec with FIPS-validated modules (validation certificates recorded in the cryptography register)

requirement: Route remote access via managed access control points.
implementation_statement: All remote access routes through two managed gateways (virtual desktop gateway and remote access service)

requirement: Authorize remote execution of privileged commands and remote access to security-relevant information.
responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Remote privileged commands require PAM checkout with approval and session recording

requirement: Authorize wireless access prior to allowing such connections
implementation_statement: Plant and office wireless in the CEE requires approved device certificates; guest wireless is separate and has no CEE route

requirement: Protect wireless access using authentication and encryption
implementation_statement: CEE wireless uses enterprise authentication with device certificates and encryption

requirement: Control connection of mobile devices.
implementation_statement: Mobile devices reach the CUI suite only when enrolled in mobile device management with a compliant posture

requirement: Encrypt CUI on mobile devices and mobile computing platforms.[23]
implementation_statement: Enclave laptops and enrolled mobile devices use full-disk or container encryption with FIPS-validated modules

requirement: Verify and control/limit connections to and use of external systems.
implementation_statement: Connections to external systems are limited to approved prime portals and supplier gateway accounts; public AI and file-sharing services are blocked from CEE endpoints and virtual desktops
evidence: Proxy category policy; external connections register

requirement: Limit use of portable storage devices on external systems.
implementation_statement: Portable storage on CEE endpoints is blocked except company-encrypted drives approved by exception

requirement: Control CUI posted or processed on publicly accessible systems.
implementation_statement: Public website and trade show content is reviewed for CUI and export control by Trade Compliance before release

requirement: Ensure that managers, systems administrators, and users of organizational systems are made aware of the security risks associated with their activities and of the applicable policies, standards, and procedures related to the security of those systems.
implementation_statement: Annual security awareness training with CUI handling and export control modules; monthly phishing simulations
evidence: Learning system completion report; phishing results

requirement: Ensure that personnel are trained to carry out their assigned information security-related duties and responsibilities.
implementation_statement: Role-based training for administrators, PLM administrators, SOC analysts, and OT engineers. Gap: 37 of 412 privileged users (9%) were overdue for annual role-based training at the 2026-06-30 cutoff
evidence: Learning system role curricula; completion report

requirement: Provide security awareness training on recognizing and reporting potential indicators of insider threat.
implementation_statement: Insider threat awareness is part of annual training for all CEE users; cleared staff also receive NISPOM insider threat training

requirement: Create and retain system audit logs and records to the extent needed to enable the monitoring, analysis, investigation, and reporting of unlawful or unauthorized system activity
implementation_statement: CEE systems send logs to the SIEM with 1 year online and 6 years in archive. Gap: 24 AZ-1 build-prep workstations were not onboarded to the SIEM

requirement: Ensure that the actions of individual system users can be uniquely traced to those users, so they can be held accountable for their actions.
responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: All CEE actions are attributable to named accounts; shared accounts are prohibited and shared MES terminals use badge plus PIN sign-in

requirement: Review and update logged events.
implementation_statement: Logged events are reviewed each year by the SOC with system owners and after major changes

requirement: Alert in the event of an audit logging process failure.
implementation_statement: SIEM alerts the SOC when a log source stops sending for more than 4 hours

requirement: Correlate audit record review, analysis, and reporting processes for investigation and response to indications of unlawful, unauthorized, suspicious, or unusual activity.
implementation_statement: 24x7 SOC correlates identity, endpoint, network, PLM, and suite logs with user behavior analytics

requirement: Provide audit record reduction and report generation to support on-demand analysis and reporting.
implementation_statement: SIEM provides on-demand queries and reports for investigations

requirement: Provide a system capability that compares and synchronizes internal system clocks with an authoritative source to generate time stamps for audit records
implementation_statement: All CEE components synchronize time with authoritative internal time sources traceable to a national time standard

requirement: Protect audit information and audit logging tools from unauthorized access, modification, and deletion.
implementation_statement: Logs are stored in write-once archive storage; SIEM access is limited by role

requirement: Limit management of audit logging functionality to a subset of privileged users.
implementation_statement: Only 6 SIEM engineers can change log settings; changes are reviewed weekly

requirement: Establish and maintain baseline configurations and inventories of organizational systems (including hardware, software, firmware, and documentation) throughout the respective system development life cycles.
implementation_statement: Documented baselines for every CEE and MOZ asset class in the configuration repository; component inventory in the CMDB. Gap: No documented baseline for the 24 AZ-1 build-prep workstations, which were installed from the printer manufacturer image

requirement: Establish and enforce security configuration settings for information technology products employed in organizational systems.
implementation_statement: Security settings enforced from the baselines through endpoint and server management; 98.6% compliance outside AZ-1. Gap: AZ-1 build-prep workstations do not meet the security configuration benchmark (local administrator rights, unneeded services)

requirement: Track, review, approve or disapprove, and log changes to organizational systems.
implementation_statement: Changes go through the change advisory board (CAB) in the IT service management tool, with emergency changes reviewed after the fact. Gap: 3 of 40 sampled CEE changes were emergency changes with no after-the-fact CAB approval

requirement: Analyze the security impact of changes prior to implementation.
implementation_statement: Every normal change includes a security impact analysis reviewed by security architecture

requirement: Define, document, approve, and enforce physical and logical access restrictions associated with changes to organizational systems.
implementation_statement: Change rights are restricted to PAM roles; infrastructure changes deploy through pipelines with approvals

requirement: Employ the principle of least functionality by configuring organizational systems to provide only essential capabilities.
implementation_statement: Baselines remove unneeded functions; virtual desktops are locked down

requirement: Restrict, disable, or prevent the use of nonessential programs, functions, ports, protocols, and services.
implementation_statement: Nonessential ports, protocols, and services are blocked by host firewalls and network policy
evidence: Host firewall policy; network rule review

requirement: Apply deny-by-exception (blacklisting) policy to prevent the use of unauthorized software or deny-all, permit-by-exception (whitelisting) policy to allow the execution of authorized software.
implementation_statement: Application allowlisting enforced on CEE endpoints and servers

requirement: Control and monitor user-installed software.
implementation_statement: Users cannot install software; requests go through the software catalog

requirement: Identify system users, processes acting on behalf of users, and devices.
responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Unique named identities for users, service accounts registered in PAM, and device certificates for managed endpoints
evidence: Identity governance report; PAM service account register

requirement: Authenticate (or verify) the identities of users, processes, or devices, as a prerequisite to allowing access to organizational systems.
responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Users authenticate with hardware security keys; devices with certificates; services with vaulted secrets

requirement: Use multifactor authentication for local and network access to privileged accounts and for network access to non-privileged accounts.[24] [25].
responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Phishing-resistant MFA (hardware security keys) for all CEE local and network access; badge plus PIN with SSO at shared MES terminals
evidence: Conditional access policy; MES sign-in configuration

requirement: Employ replay-resistant authentication mechanisms for network access to privileged and non-privileged accounts.
responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Authentication uses replay-resistant protocols (FIDO2, Kerberos, TLS)

requirement: Prevent reuse of identifiers for a defined period.
responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Identifiers are never reused; disabled accounts are retained for 2 years

requirement: Disable identifiers after a defined period of inactivity.
responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Accounts inactive for 45 days are disabled automatically

requirement: Enforce a minimum password complexity and change of characters when new passwords are created.
responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Passwords (where still used) meet length and complexity rules; most users are passwordless with security keys

requirement: Prohibit password reuse for a specified number of generations.
responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Password history of 24

requirement: Allow temporary password use for system logons with an immediate change to a permanent password.
responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Temporary passwords force change at first use

requirement: Store and transmit only cryptographically-protected passwords.
responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Passwords are stored hashed and transmitted only over encrypted channels; service secrets are vaulted

requirement: Obscure feedback of authentication information
responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Authentication feedback is masked on all sign-in pages

requirement: Establish an operational incident-handling capability for organizational systems that includes preparation, detection, analysis, containment, recovery, and user response activities.
implementation_statement: 24x7 SOC with incident response plan, playbooks (including the P08 CUI exfiltration runbook), and a forensic retainer

requirement: Track, document, and report incidents to designated officials and/or authorities both internal and external to the organization.
implementation_statement: Incidents tracked in the case system; DFARS reportability decisions recorded by the Vice President, Contracts; DIBNet reports filed with medium assurance certificates

requirement: Test the organizational incident response capability.
implementation_statement: Incident response tested by the 2026-04-15 DIBNet drill and the 2026-04-22 tabletop

requirement: Perform maintenance on organizational systems.[26].
implementation_statement: Maintenance is scheduled through the service management tool and the OT maintenance system

requirement: Provide controls on the tools, techniques, mechanisms, and personnel used to conduct system maintenance.
implementation_statement: Maintenance tools are company-owned or inspected; vendor technicians are escorted and use company tools

requirement: Ensure equipment removed for off-site maintenance is sanitized of any CUI.
implementation_statement: Equipment leaving for off-site repair is sanitized or its storage removed

requirement: Check media containing diagnostic and test programs for malicious code before the media are used in organizational systems.
implementation_statement: Diagnostic media are scanned at a kiosk before use

requirement: Require multifactor authentication to establish nonlocal maintenance sessions via external network connections and terminate such connections when nonlocal maintenance is complete.
implementation_statement: Remote maintenance by 5 of 6 equipment manufacturers goes through PAM with company MFA and session recording. Gap: One printer manufacturer at AZ-1 connects through its own remote support tool without company MFA or session recording
evidence: PAM vendor session records; remote access register

requirement: Supervise the maintenance activities of maintenance personnel without required access authorization.
implementation_statement: Maintenance personnel without access are escorted and supervised

requirement: Protect (i.e., physically control and securely store) system media containing CUI, both paper and digital.
implementation_statement: Printed CUI is kept in controlled cabinets in cells and engineering areas; digital media are encrypted

requirement: Limit access to CUI on system media to authorized users
implementation_statement: Access to CUI media limited by role; printing to badge-release printers only

requirement: Sanitize or destroy system media containing CUI before disposal or release for reuse.
implementation_statement: Media and equipment with CUI are sanitized per NIST SP 800-88 or destroyed by a certified vendor with certificates. Gap: 2 of 25 sampled machine controller drives sent for repair had no sanitization record

requirement: Mark media with necessary CUI markings and distribution limitations.[27]
implementation_statement: CUI banners added by PLM and print templates; customer distribution statements kept

requirement: Control access to media containing CUI and maintain accountability for media during transport outside of controlled areas.
implementation_statement: Physical CUI shipped only by approved couriers in sealed packaging with tracking; logs kept by shipping

requirement: Implement cryptographic mechanisms to protect the confidentiality of CUI stored on digital media during transport unless otherwise protected by alternative physical safeguards.
implementation_statement: Portable media and laptops use FIPS-validated encryption

requirement: Control the use of removable media on system components.
implementation_statement: Removable media blocked on CEE endpoints except approved encrypted drives. Gap: AZ-1 printers are loaded from USB drives written on build-prep workstations; 6 of 25 sampled transfers skipped the scanning kiosk

requirement: Prohibit the use of portable storage devices when such devices have no identifiable owner.
implementation_statement: Only labeled, inventoried company drives are permitted; unknown drives are blocked by device control

requirement: Protect the confidentiality of backup CUI at storage locations.
implementation_statement: Backups are encrypted and stored in separate immutable accounts with restricted access

requirement: Screen individuals prior to authorizing access to organizational systems containing CUI.
implementation_statement: Background checks before access; U.S.-person verification for CEE access
evidence: HR screening records; export screening log

requirement: Ensure that organizational systems containing CUI are protected during and after personnel actions such as terminations and transfers
implementation_statement: HR separations disable access automatically; transfers trigger access review. Gap: Same as 3.1.1: 2 contractor separations disabled late

requirement: Limit physical access to organizational systems, equipment, and the respective operating environments to authorized individuals.
implementation_statement: Badge access to CEE areas, server rooms, and plant engineering areas; quarterly badge access review

requirement: Protect and monitor the physical facility and support infrastructure for organizational systems.
implementation_statement: Monitored cameras and alarms at all sites; data centers have 24x7 security

requirement: Escort visitors and monitor visitor activity.
implementation_statement: Visitors are escorted in CUI areas and recorded in the visitor management system. Gap: At TX-1, 2 of 10 sampled visitors had no escort recorded in CUI areas (cannot be on a CMMC POA&M)

requirement: Maintain audit logs of physical access.
implementation_statement: Physical access logs from badge and visitor systems are kept 3 years. Gap: At TX-1, 2 of 10 sampled visitor entries had no sign-out (cannot be on a CMMC POA&M)

requirement: Control and manage physical access devices.
implementation_statement: Badges, keys, and lock codes are managed by site security with quarterly inventory

requirement: Enforce safeguarding measures for CUI at alternate work sites.
implementation_statement: Remote work with CUI is allowed only through virtual desktops on company devices; printing at home is blocked

requirement: Periodically assess the risk to organizational operations (including mission, functions, image, or reputation), organizational assets, and individuals, resulting from the operation of organizational systems and the associated processing, storage, or transmission of CUI
implementation_statement: Annual enterprise risk assessment (P01) using SP 800-30 Rev. 1, integrated with ERM

requirement: Scan for vulnerabilities in organizational systems and applications periodically and when new vulnerabilities affecting those systems and applications are identified.
implementation_statement: Authenticated vulnerability scans of CEE assets weekly and after major changes

requirement: Remediate vulnerabilities in accordance with risk assessments.
implementation_statement: Remediation SLAs by severity (critical 15 days, high 30 days). Gap: 9 of 60 sampled critical and high findings were remediated past SLA, mostly in the virtual desktop image refresh cycle

requirement: Periodically assess the security controls in organizational systems to determine if the controls are effective in their application.
implementation_statement: Annual control assessment by Internal Audit (P07) plus continuous monitoring

requirement: Develop and implement plans of action designed to correct deficiencies and reduce or eliminate vulnerabilities in organizational systems.
implementation_statement: POA&M in the GRC platform, reviewed monthly by the CMMC Program Office and quarterly by the executive risk committee

requirement: Monitor security controls on an ongoing basis to ensure the continued effectiveness of the controls.
implementation_statement: Continuous monitoring through configuration compliance, vulnerability, and SIEM dashboards reported monthly

requirement: Develop, document, and periodically update system security plans that describe system boundaries, system environments of operation, how security requirements are implemented, and the relationships with or connections to other systems.[28]
point_value: No point value; SSP absence prevents assessment (170.24(c)(2)(i)(B)(5))
implementation_statement: CEE SSP v3.1 (2026-09-14) and MOZ SSP describe boundaries, environments, and requirement implementation, updated after the AZ-1 change

requirement: Monitor, control, and protect communications (i.e., information transmitted or received by organizational systems) at the external boundaries and key internal boundaries of organizational systems.
implementation_statement: Boundary firewalls at each site and cloud network security policies monitor and control CEE traffic. Gap: At AZ-1, the build-prep workstation and printer segment was reachable from the corporate network over file-sharing ports

requirement: Employ architectural designs, software development techniques, and systems engineering principles that promote effective information security within organizational systems.
implementation_statement: Security architecture standards and design reviews for CEE changes (zero-trust access, segmentation, encryption)

requirement: Separate user functionality from system management functionality.
implementation_statement: Management interfaces are reachable only from PAM jump hosts

requirement: Prevent unauthorized and unintended information transfer via shared system resources.
implementation_statement: Virtual desktops are non-persistent; shared resources are cleared between sessions

requirement: Implement subnetworks for publicly accessible system components that are physically or logically separated from internal networks.
implementation_statement: The CUI exchange gateway sits in a separate subnet with only required flows to internal services

requirement: Deny network communications traffic by default and allow network communications traffic by exception (i.e., deny all, permit by exception).
implementation_statement: Deny-by-default rules with documented exceptions at every CEE boundary

requirement: Prevent remote devices from simultaneously establishing non-remote connections with organizational systems and communicating via some other connection to resources in external networks (i.e., split tunneling).
implementation_statement: Split tunneling is disabled on enclave laptops

requirement: Implement cryptographic mechanisms to prevent unauthorized disclosure of CUI during transmission unless otherwise protected by alternative physical safeguards.
implementation_statement: CUI in transit is protected by TLS 1.2 or higher and IPsec using FIPS-validated modules

requirement: Terminate network connections associated with communications sessions at the end of the sessions or after a defined period of inactivity.
implementation_statement: Sessions end on logout or after idle timeouts

requirement: Establish and manage cryptographic keys for cryptography employed in organizational systems.
implementation_statement: Customer-managed keys in the cloud key management service with rotation and dual control

requirement: Employ FIPS-validated cryptography when used to protect the confidentiality of CUI.
implementation_statement: FIPS-validated cryptography confirmed for every CUI path, including the CUI exchange gateway and plant IPsec tunnels (certificate numbers in the cryptography register)

requirement: Prohibit remote activation of collaborative computing devices and provide indication of devices in use to users present at the device.[29].
implementation_statement: Collaborative device activation is user-initiated with visible indicators; remote activation disabled

requirement: Control and monitor the use of mobile code.
implementation_statement: Mobile code controlled by browser policy and allowlisting

requirement: Control and monitor the use of Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) technologies.
implementation_statement: VoIP phones in CEE areas on a separate voice segment with restricted management

requirement: Protect the authenticity of communications sessions.
implementation_statement: Session authenticity protected by TLS with certificate validation and token binding where supported

requirement: Protect the confidentiality of CUI at rest.
implementation_statement: CUI at rest encrypted in the suite, PLM storage, endpoints, and backups with FIPS-validated modules

requirement: Identify, report, and correct system flaws in a timely manner.
implementation_statement: Patching by severity SLA with monthly maintenance windows. Gap: Same as 3.11.3: 9 of 60 sampled findings fixed past SLA

requirement: Provide protection from malicious code at designated locations within organizational systems.
implementation_statement: EDR on all CEE endpoints and servers

requirement: Monitor system security alerts and advisories and take action in response.
implementation_statement: SOC receives advisories from DoD, CISA, prime, and commercial feeds and tracks actions

requirement: Update malicious code protection mechanisms when new releases are available.
implementation_statement: EDR updates automatically

requirement: Perform periodic scans of organizational systems and real-time scans of files from external sources as files are downloaded, opened, or executed.
implementation_statement: Real-time scanning by EDR; files from the gateway scanned on arrival

requirement: Monitor organizational systems, including inbound and outbound communications traffic, to detect attacks and indicators of potential attacks.
implementation_statement: SOC monitors inbound and outbound traffic, with alerts for bulk downloads and unusual transfers

requirement: Identify unauthorized use of organizational systems.
implementation_statement: User behavior analytics flags unusual access to PLM and the suite

requirement: Organization-owned resources only (SP 800-172 requirement with DoD parameters; see 32 CFR 170.14(c)(4) table 1)
responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: CEE access only from company-owned, managed devices; personal devices are blocked by device compliance checks

requirement: Secure information transfer between security domains (SP 800-172 requirement with DoD parameters; see 32 CFR 170.14(c)(4) table 1)
implementation_statement: Transfers between the CEE, the MOZ, and the corporate network go through the CUI exchange gateway or approved data diodes at 5 plants. Gap: AZ-1 and FL-3 move files between domains by USB and file shares; no secure transfer solution there

requirement: Threat-focused awareness training (SP 800-172 requirement with DoD parameters; see 32 CFR 170.14(c)(4) table 1)
implementation_statement: Training at hire, annually, and after significant events covers social engineering, advanced persistent threat tradecraft, and suspicious behaviors; content refreshed 2026-02

requirement: Practical exercises in training (SP 800-172 requirement with DoD parameters; see 32 CFR 170.14(c)(4) table 1)
implementation_statement: Monthly phishing simulations for all users. Gap: No role-tailored practical exercises for privileged users and specialized roles; supervisors do not receive results

requirement: Authoritative component repository (SP 800-172 requirement with DoD parameters; see 32 CFR 170.14(c)(4) table 1)
implementation_statement: The CMDB is the declared authoritative source for CEE and MOZ components. Gap: CMDB accuracy 92% in sampling (5 of 60 sampled assets missing or wrong)

requirement: Automated detection and quarantine of misconfigured or unauthorized components (SP 800-172 requirement with DoD parameters; see 32 CFR 170.14(c)(4) table 1)
implementation_statement: NAC quarantines unknown devices at 5 sites. Gap: No automated quarantine at FL-3 and AZ-1

requirement: Automated discovery and inventory (SP 800-172 requirement with DoD parameters; see 32 CFR 170.14(c)(4) table 1)
implementation_statement: Automated discovery runs at 5 sites and in the cloud subscriptions. Gap: No automated discovery of OT segments at FL-3 and AZ-1

requirement: Bidirectional cryptographic device authentication (SP 800-172 requirement with DoD parameters; see 32 CFR 170.14(c)(4) table 1)
implementation_statement: 802.1X with device certificates at FL-1, FL-2, GA-1, AL-1, TX-1; cloud workloads use mutual TLS. Gap: Not deployed at FL-3 and AZ-1

requirement: Block unknown or misconfigured components (SP 800-172 requirement with DoD parameters; see 32 CFR 170.14(c)(4) table 1)
implementation_statement: Device compliance checks for user access; NAC and manual approval for OT connections at all sites

requirement: 24/7 security operations center (SP 800-172 requirement with DoD parameters; see 32 CFR 170.14(c)(4) table 1)
implementation_statement: In-house SOC operates 24/7 at FL-1 and TX-1 with on-call staff

requirement: Cyber incident response team deployable within 24 hours (SP 800-172 requirement with DoD parameters; see 32 CFR 170.14(c)(4) table 1)
implementation_statement: Incident response team with travel kits; deployment tested to TX-1 in 2026-04 (on site in 9 hours)

requirement: Protect systems when adverse information develops (SP 800-172 requirement with DoD parameters; see 32 CFR 170.14(c)(4) table 1)
implementation_statement: Adverse information about cleared employees is reported under NISPOM (32 CFR 117.8(c)) and triggers access review. Gap: No process links adverse information about uncleared CEE users (about 3,100) to access decisions

requirement: Threat intelligence in risk assessment (SP 800-172 requirement with DoD parameters; see 32 CFR 170.14(c)(4) table 1)
implementation_statement: Commercial, open-source, DoD (DC3 DIB collaborative information sharing), and prime threat intelligence informs the P01 assessment and architecture decisions

requirement: Cyber threat hunting (SP 800-172 requirement with DoD parameters; see 32 CFR 170.14(c)(4) table 1)
implementation_statement: Analysts hunt when intelligence warrants. Gap: Hunts are ad hoc and not documented; no hunt calendar or records of scope and findings

requirement: Advanced automation and analytics (SP 800-172 requirement with DoD parameters; see 32 CFR 170.14(c)(4) table 1)
implementation_statement: User behavior analytics and automated triage support SOC analysts

requirement: Security solution rationale in the SSP (SP 800-172 requirement with DoD parameters; see 32 CFR 170.14(c)(4) table 1)
implementation_statement: The CEE SSP records selected solutions for major controls. Gap: Rationale and risk determination are not recorded for each security solution

requirement: Annual effectiveness assessment of security solutions (SP 800-172 requirement with DoD parameters; see 32 CFR 170.14(c)(4) table 1)
implementation_statement: Internal Audit and the SOC assess security solution effectiveness annually and after significant threat intelligence (P07; 2026-04 purple team)

requirement: Supply chain risk response (SP 800-172 requirement with DoD parameters; see 32 CFR 170.14(c)(4) table 1)
implementation_statement: Supplier tiering and contract security terms; monitoring of tier-1 IT and OT vendors. Gap: Supplier CMMC status verified for 176 of 380 CUI suppliers; no response playbook for component supply chain events

requirement: Supply chain risk management plan (SP 800-172 requirement with DoD parameters; see 32 CFR 170.14(c)(4) table 1)
implementation_statement: Supply chain risk management plan for purchased material (quality and counterfeit parts). Gap: The plan does not cover system components and IT or OT services; no annual update rule

requirement: Annual penetration testing (SP 800-172 requirement with DoD parameters; see 32 CFR 170.14(c)(4) table 1)
implementation_statement: Annual external penetration test of corporate systems (2026-03). Gap: No penetration test of the CEE since 2025-06-12

requirement: Physical or logical isolation (SP 800-172 requirement with DoD parameters; see 32 CFR 170.14(c)(4) table 1)
implementation_statement: The CEE is logically isolated in its own government-community tenant and network segments; MOZ segments isolated from corporate at 6 of 7 sites

requirement: Root of trust or signature verification for critical software (SP 800-172 requirement with DoD parameters; see 32 CFR 170.14(c)(4) table 1)
implementation_statement: Secure boot and signed drivers on endpoints; code signing enforced for scripts. Gap: No integrity verification on MES and DNC servers and AZ-1 build-prep workstations

requirement: Specialized assets in scope or segregated (SP 800-172 requirement with DoD parameters; see 32 CFR 170.14(c)(4) table 1)
implementation_statement: CNC machines, CMMs, autoclaves, and test cells are segregated in MOZ segments at 6 sites. Gap: AZ-1 printers share a segment reachable from the corporate network (cannot be on a Level 3 POA&M)

requirement: Threat indicators guide detection and hunting (SP 800-172 requirement with DoD parameters; see 32 CFR 170.14(c)(4) table 1)
implementation_statement: Indicators from DoD, commercial, and open sources are loaded into the SIEM and EDR automatically
